mcqs.q: An impression is a ___ likeness and a cast is a ___ likeness.
mcqs.explain: The impression is the negative imprint; the cast poured into it is the positive reproduction.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal requisite of an impression material?
opts: It should set without distorting or tearing on removal and stay dimensionally stable until poured
It should be toxic to inhibit bacteria
It should expand greatly on setting
mcqs.explain: Ideal materials adapt yet stay in the tray, set in reasonable time, resist distortion/tearing, remain dimensionally stable, are cost-effective and biocompatible.

mcqs.q: Which group of impression materials is RIGID (inelastic)?
opts: Impression plaster, compound, wax and ZOE
mcqs.explain: Rigid: plaster, compound, wax, ZOE. Elastic: hydrocolloids (alginate/agar) and elastomers.

mcqs.q: A material that sets by a reversible PHYSICAL reaction is termed:
mcqs.explain: Reversible/physical set = thermoplastic (e.g. compound, wax); irreversible/chemical = thermoset (e.g. plaster, ZOE, alginate).

opts: Type-1 gypsum (calcium sulfate hemihydrate) with modifiers
mcqs.explain: Impression plaster is modified type-1 gypsum; hemihydrate + water → dihydrate on setting.

mcqs.q: Why can impression plaster NOT record undercuts?
opts: It is rigid/inelastic and would break
It is too viscous to reach them
mcqs.explain: Being rigid and non-elastic, plaster fractures if withdrawn over an undercut.

mcqs.q: Two properties that make plaster less suitable as an impression material are:
opts: Prolonged setting time (~15 min) and setting expansion
mcqs.explain: Its long set (~15 min) and setting expansion are drawbacks (expansion controlled with an anti-expansion solution).

mcqs.q: Impression waxes (e.g. Iowa/Korecta wax) are chiefly used to:
opts: Correct small imperfections and border extension of an impression
Take a full primary edentulous impression alone
Record deep undercuts on natural teeth
Serve as a permanent denture base
mcqs.explain: Corrective waxes fill defects, correct borders and register soft-tissue detail as a veneer over an impression.

opts: A reversible physical process — used warm (~45°C) then cooled to a rigid mass
mcqs.explain: Compound is thermoplastic: softened by heat (~45°C) and rigid when cooled to mouth temperature.

mcqs.q: In low-fusing (Type I) impression compound, the STICK form is mainly used for:
opts: Border molding of a custom tray
The full edentulous impression in a stock tray
mcqs.explain: Type I cakes take edentulous impressions; sticks are used for border molding/peripheral tracing.

mcqs.q: Prolonged immersion of impression compound in the water bath makes it:
mcqs.explain: Over-immersion leaches components, leaving the compound brittle and grainy.

mcqs.q: Which is a disadvantage of impression compound?
opts: It does not reproduce fine surface detail and cannot record undercuts
It is too elastic for edentulous ridges
It sets instantly and cannot be re-adapted
mcqs.explain: Compound gives poor fine detail, distorts, and cannot handle undercuts; but it is non-toxic and re-adaptable.

mcqs.q: Zinc-oxide eugenol impression paste (ADA No. 16) is supplied as:
opts: A two-paste system (base with zinc oxide, catalyst with eugenol) that forms a chelate
A single powder mixed with water
mcqs.explain: The base (ZnO + vegetable oil) reacts with the catalyst (eugenol + rosin/fillers) to form a zinc-eugenolate chelate.

mcqs.q: For a ZOE impression, the impression should be SEATED in the mouth before the:
mcqs.explain: Seat before the initial set (3–6 min); withdraw only after the final set (10–15 min).

mcqs.q: A recognized USE of ZOE impression paste is:
opts: Final impressions of edentulous ridges with minor or no undercuts
Impressions of teeth with deep undercuts
Making diagnostic casts of dentate arches
As a permanent luting cement for crowns
mcqs.explain: ZOE is used for final edentulous impressions (no undercuts), wash impressions, temporary relines and perio packs.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of ZOE impression paste is that:
opts: The eugenol can cause a burning sensation and tissue irritation
It cannot record any surface detail
It sets far too quickly to use
mcqs.explain: ZOE gives excellent detail and is stable, but it is sticky and its eugenol can irritate/burn tissues.

saqs.q: List four ideal requisites of an impression material.
saqs.a: Fluid enough to adapt to the oral tissues; viscous enough to be contained in the tray; sets to a rubbery/rigid solid in a reasonable time; does not distort or tear on removal; dimensionally stable at least until the cast is poured; cost-effective; and biocompatible.

saqs.q: Classify impression materials by elasticity and by setting mechanism, with an example of each.
saqs.a: By elasticity: rigid/inelastic (impression plaster, compound, wax, ZOE) and elastic (hydrocolloids — alginate/agar — and elastomers — polysulfide, polyether, silicones). By setting: irreversible/chemical (thermoset), e.g. plaster, ZOE, alginate; and reversible/physical (thermoplastic), e.g. impression compound, wax, agar.

saqs.q: Describe impression plaster: its nature, why it cannot record undercuts, and two disadvantages.
saqs.a: Impression plaster is modified type-1 gypsum (calcium sulfate hemihydrate) — irreversible, non-elastic and low-viscosity; hemihydrate + water → dihydrate on setting. It cannot record undercuts because, being rigid, it breaks on withdrawal. Disadvantages include prolonged setting (~15 min) and setting expansion, being washed away in wet mouths, exothermic heat/nausea, and needing a separator (surface inaccuracy).

saqs.q: Describe impression compound (Type I vs Type II) and its setting behaviour.
saqs.a: Compound (ADA No. 3) is reversible, non-elastic and high-viscosity; it cannot record undercuts. Type I (lower fusing): cakes for edentulous impressions and sticks (colour-coded by softening temperature) for border molding. Type II (higher fusing): tray-adaptation material used for a primary impression that then supports a thin second material. It is a reversible physical set — softened warm (~45°C) in a thermostatic water bath and rigid when cooled to 37°C.

saqs.q: For ZOE impression paste, give its composition (base and catalyst) and its two setting times.
saqs.a: Two-paste system: base paste = zinc oxide (~87%) + vegetable oil; catalyst paste = eugenol (oil of cloves) + polymerized rosin + fillers + lanolin + resinous balsam + accelerators; they react to form a chelate. Setting times: initial 3–6 minutes (seat before the initial set) and final 10–15 minutes (withdraw at the final set).
